Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ was admitted to the hospital with nausea and vomiting, 
fever and flushing concerned for a wide differential diagnoses.  
During her work up, a bone marrow biopsy displayed acute blast 
crisis from her chronic myelogenous leukemia.  Initial 
immunophenotyping suggested biphenotypic blast crisis.  She was 
treated presumptively for Strongyloides with Ivermectin x2 days 
given her travel history & country of origin, prior to 
initiating chemotherapy.  In addition, her PPD turned positive 
and review of her chest CT suggested old Tuberculosis.  
Treatment was deferred per ID until the chemotherapy effects on 
her liver could be evaluated. 

The patient was started on HyperCVAD with intrathecal 
Methotrexate and dasatinib.  The day after Hyper-CVAD initiation 
repeat/further immunophenotyping revealed that it was in fact a 
myleoblastic crisis.  She was switched to 7+3 induction regimen 
without dasatinib.  The patient's course was complicated by 
neutropenia and intermittent fever, later found to be due to GNR 
bacteremia and PNA. Cultures finalized as Leptortrichia. Patient 
was treated with broad spectrum antimicrobials including 
Meropenem, Vancomycin, Flagyl, Micafungin and Acylovir.  Her 
hickmann line was removed and replaced with a PICC. She was 
treated with IV antibiotics until her counts recovered and she 
was afebrile. She was discharged on oral flagyl as this bacteria 
usually is susceptible to this antibiotic per case reports. She 
will complete a two weeek course as an outpatient. Chest CT 
revealed improvement of her pneumonia. In addition, the patient 
developed intractable nausea and vomiting, which, poorly 
controlled, led ultimately to hematemesis found to be due to 
___ tears. On return from the ICU, the patient's 
nausea was well controlled on PPI, Zofran, Zyprexa.  She had no 
more episodes of hematemesis but continued to have fevers and 
neutropenia. Fevers abated and counts recovered. Decision was 
made for patient to complete antibiotics as outpatient for two 
week course of po flagyl and return for transplant. She will 
restart destanib as an outpatient. Counts will be checked two 
days post-discharge.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  ___ woman with acute myelogenous leukemia who
requires triple-lumen tunneled catheter for chemotherapy.

FELLOW:  Dr. ___.

STAFF RADIOLOGIST:  Dr. ___ supervised the procedure.

SEDATION:  Fentanyl IV 50 mg.  1% lidocaine for local anesthesia.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  After review of the risks and benefits of the
procedure as well as conscious sedation, informed consent was obtained via a
___ interpreter.  The patient was brought to the angiography suite and
placed supine on the imaging table.  The right side of the neck and upper
chest were prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  Access was
obtained into the right internal jugular vein with a micropuncture needle
under ultrasound guidance.  Hard copy ultrasound images were obtained before
and after access.  A 0.018 wire was placed through the needle and advanced
into the SVC using flouroscopic guidance.  The needle was removed and replaced
with a micropuncture sheath, which was used to upsize the wire to a short
___ wire.

Next, a subcutaneous tunnel was created on the upper anterior chest wall,
through which a new 12.5 triple-lumen catheter was pulled.  A peel-away sheath
was placed over the wire and the catheter was fed through the sheath as the
sheath was peeled away.  The final position of the tip is in the SVC.  The
catheter length is 12 cm.  All three ports flushed and aspirated easily.  The
catheter was sutured to the skin and a sterile dressing was applied.  There
were no immediate complications.

IMPRESSION:  12.5 ___ triple-lumen tunneled Hickman catheter placed via
right IJ access with tip in the SVC.  The catheter is ready to use.

2.  Ground-glass nodular opacity in right lower lobe,likely small focus of

HISTORY:  ___ male with CML status post chemotherapy, history of
___ tear complicated by UGIB, now with chest pain radiating to the
back.  Please evaluate for aortic dissection, signs of pericarditis, signs of
esophagitis, worsening pneumonia or any other etiology of chest pain.

COMPARISON:  Prior chest CT study obtained on ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT of the chest was obtained before and after administration of
intravenous contrast.  Images were reformatted in the axial, sagittal, coronal
and oblique planes.

FINDINGS:  Right-sided central line is in place with tip terminating in SVC.
Aorta is normal in size without evidence of dissection.  The pulmonary
arteries are unremarkable, without evidence of thrombus.  The esophagus is
unremarkable.

Previously described pneumonia in right middle and upper lobe represents
interval improvement.  A 5-mm nodule in the right lower lobe is unchanged
compared to the prior study. No new areas of consolidation.  No pleural
effusion.

Heart size is within normal limits. Unchanged small pericardial effusion
persists.

Previously noted calcified lymph nodes in mediastinal and hilar stations are
again noted. Calcification in the right breast is unchanged.

Limited images of the upper abdominal organs is unremarkable except for
evidence for cholecystectomy, and calcified granuloma in the spleen.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  Degenerative changes in spine.  No worrisome lytic or
blastic bony lesions are identified.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No evidence of aortic dissection.
2.  Stable small pericardial effusion.
3.  Interval improvement of right-sided pneumonia.
4.  Small 5-mm nodule in right lower lobe that is unchanged compared to prior
study.  If patient has history of smoking or any other known risk factors,
initial followup CT in six months is suggested according to ___
guidelines.
